The thoughts behind the circle.

The founder

Ms. Sumi Rengaraj

M.S. Psychology

Founder, Sphere Women

An international entrepreneur and wellness practitioner, Ms. Sumi Rengaraj brings together her expertise in business, psychology, and holistic wellness. As a Yoga and Pranayama Instructor and Certified Emotional Intelligence Practitioner, she is passionate about nurturing emotional well-being, mindful living, and a healthier, more connected community.

As the founder of Sphere Women, her vision is to bring holistic wellness practices back into the community, reconnecting people with the ancient wisdom and healing traditions rooted in India. Through Sphere, she aspires to share these time-honoured practices with the world, giving back to the community and nurturing a deeper connection between people, nature, and the earth. Her mission is to make wellness accessible, meaningful, and an integral part of everyday life.

Why The Sphere?

Because a woman needs a space that is just for her.

  • You may be a founder.
  • A mother.
  • A leader.
  • A daughter.
  • A partner.
  • A friend.

You may be building something extraordinary.

But beyond every role you hold, there is you.

The Sphere exists to create a little more room for that woman.

A space that feels like yours

Wellness, beyond the usual.

We believe wellness is more than a workout, a treatment or a moment of escape.

  • It is how you feel when you leave a room.
  • The people you meet.
  • The conversations you have.
  • The rituals you return to.
  • And the space you create for yourself amidst everything else.

The Sphere brings these moments together through carefully curated experiences designed exclusively for women.

Is wellness a luxury or a necessity?

We believe it is a necessity.

For a woman constantly giving her time, energy and attention to everyone around her, taking care of herself can often become the last item on the list.

The Sphere challenges that idea. We believe taking care of yourself isn't indulgence. It is part of living well.

And sometimes, choosing yourself begins with something as simple as showing up for an hour.
